caption:
Part of the Cult Classics series, Atlantis (2001) came up multiple times in my recent Shows → Books requests video, and I couldn’t agree more. My original dvd is still floating around somewhere in The Library… I’ll get my Chief of Security on that, as soon as he finishes his nap 🐾

Book List:
To Sleep in a Sea of Stars, Christopher Paolini
The Adventures of Amina al-Sirafi, Shannon Chakraborty
The Starless Sea, Erin Morgenstern
The Stardust Grail, Yume Kitasei
author: Annaberlin.writes
transcript: You're looking for Atlantis book recs? I have you covered. If you're wanting more lost civilization, ancient tech, and big discoveries, you need to sleep in a sea of stars. But if you're looking for misfit crew adventure, artifacts, and daring deeds, The Adventures of Amina al-Sarafi, maybe you're more scholar with a dream discovering secrets in an impossible world, that's The Starless Sea. But if you really just want the archaeological mysteries of Atlantis but in space, you should read The Stardust Grail. Thank you for visiting the Bridge Library and follow for more writer-approved book recs.
title: Atlantis (2001) Inspired Book Recommendations
one_liner: A librarian recommends four books matching the themes of the animated film Atlantis.
key_points: 'To Sleep in a Sea of Stars' for lost civilization and ancient tech vibes
'Adventures of Amina al-Sirafi' for misfit crew adventures and daring artifact hunts
'The Starless Sea' for scholars uncovering secrets in a mysterious world
'The Stardust Grail' for archaeological mysteries set in space
